transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… work, mostly. We got a new operations manager, and he’s been picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. Since then I just can’t seem to leave it there. I come home wound up, I snap at my husband, and I lie awake going over meetings in my head. Then at work I’m second-guessing quality calls I used to make without thinking.
Do you find yourself worrying about work even when you're not there, like when you're at home or trying to sleep?

Yes. I try not to, but it follows me home. I’ll be lying in bed replaying what was said in meetings, wondering if I handled things right. Ever since the new manager started picking apart my procedures, I just… can’t really shut it off.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about things other than work, like everyday situations or responsibilities?
Not really… I mean, I worry about normal things like anyone does, but it doesn’t stick in my head the same way. It’s mostly work.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, trouble relaxing, or muscle tension since all this started?

Yeah… I do come home pretty wound up. It’s hard to relax after work, and then I’ll be lying there replaying meetings in my head. I don’t know about muscle tension exactly, but I feel… keyed up, I guess.
Do you feel like you can control the worrying about work, or does it feel like it just keeps going no matter what you do?

It feels like it keeps going, honestly. I try to tell myself to drop it, but then I’m back replaying what the manager said or second-guessing calls I made that used to be routine for me. It’s hard to leave it there.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly, like a panic attack?
No… I don’t think so. I get upset or wound up, but not like something that suddenly hits me all at once.
Outside of work, do you ever find yourself feeling unusually worried or on edge about things that wouldn’t have bothered you before?

Mostly it’s tied to work. I mean… maybe I’m more on edge at home than I used to be, like I’ll snap at my husband over little things. But it usually starts with stuff from work still running through my head.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain tasks or responsibilities at work because of the stress or worry?

Yeah… I have. I’ve kind of pulled back from some meetings I’m supposed to be in, and I’ve missed some internal deadlines. I don’t like saying that, but my work record’s taken a hit. At home too, I’m not keeping up with our usual evening stuff, and my husband and I have been arguing more.
Would you say your anxiety began around the same time the new manager started at work, and does it feel like a reaction to the changes they’ve brought?

Yes… I think so. It really started after the new operations manager came in and started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. Since then I just… I can’t leave it at work. I come home wound up, replay meetings at night, and then I’m second-guessing quality calls I used to make without much trouble.
Even outside of thinking about the manager and the changes at work, do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried in other areas of your life that you didn’t used to?

Not really in a broad way, no. It’s mostly… it starts with work. Since the new manager began questioning the procedures I’ve always used, I come home still wound up, and then I’ll snap at my husband or lie there replaying meetings. But I don’t think I’m suddenly worrying about everything else for no reason.
Even when work isn’t on your mind, do you find yourself feeling more anxious or worried than you used to in general, like something is off or you’re just not at ease?

Not really… not in general. It’s more like when work gets stirred up in my head. Since the new operations manager started picking apart my inspection procedures, I come home wound up, and then I’m short with my husband or up at night replaying meetings. If work isn’t in it, I don’t think I’m just anxious out of nowhere.
Even when you're not thinking about work or the new manager, do you ever feel like you're on edge or overly concerned about things in your personal life that you weren't before?

No… not really personal-life things by themselves. It’s more that I bring work home with me. I’m wound up after those meetings, and then I’ll snap at my husband or lie there replaying what was said. It all seems to start with the new manager questioning how I do the inspections.
Do you find that your worry about work feels excessive or more intense than it should be, even considering the changes with the new manager?

Yeah… maybe. I mean, the manager is changing things, so some worry makes sense, but it feels like I can’t shut it off. I come home still wound up, and then the next day I’m second-guessing quality calls I used to make without thinking. So… yes, it feels bigger than it should.

Even when you’re not thinking about work or the new manager, do you ever find yourself feeling anxious or worried about other things in your life, like personal relationships or future events, more than you used to?

No… I don’t think it’s really about other things. It’s mostly work. Since the new operations manager started picking apart how I do inspections, I just can’t seem to leave it there. I come home wound up, and then it spills over… like I’m short with my husband or up at night replaying meetings.
Even when you’re not thinking about work or the new manager, do you ever feel a general sense of worry or anxiety that seems to come up on its own, not tied to any specific problem or situation?

Not really on its own, no. It’s usually tied back to work… the new manager picking apart the inspection procedures. I come home wound up, and then I’m lying there replaying meetings or second-guessing things I used to just handle. It doesn’t feel like it comes from nowhere.
